criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject declares or advertises mandatory requirements; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when no mandatory requirements are declared or advertised, recorded as 'no mandatory requirements declared or advertised'
criteria.expected: Mandatory declared or advertised requirements are satisfied by code or configuration evidence
criteria.method: Freeze the requirements registry, grade each mandatory requirement Pass, Partial, Fail, or Unknown against code and configuration evidence, then derive the level mechanically from the coverage ratio c over graded mandatory requirements (Pass 1, Partial 1/2, Fail 0)
criteria.sufficiency: Every mandatory requirement graded against inspected code or configuration; missing evidence grades the requirement Unknown, never Pass. Resolves UNKNOWN when graded mandatory requirements are at most half of all mandatory requirements, and NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when no mandatory requirements are declared or advertised

levels.PASS: Coverage ratio c >= 95% of graded mandatory requirements
levels.P75: Coverage ratio 85% <= c < 95% of graded mandatory requirements
levels.P50: Coverage ratio 70% <= c < 85% of graded mandatory requirements
levels.P25: Coverage ratio 50% <= c < 70% of graded mandatory requirements
levels.FAIL: Coverage ratio c < 50% of graded mandatory requirements

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject advertises workflows in documentation, specification, or contract surfaces; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject advertises no workflows, since the journey-trace denominator is empty
criteria.expected: Every advertised workflow traces end to end through its declared producer and consumer hops with all hops conforming
criteria.method: Journey trace per advertised workflow from documentation and profile claims: walk the declared path through each producer and consumer hop, record each hop as conforming, failing, or unresolvable, and classify the workflow as conforming, deviating (declared outcome reached with a non-conforming hop), failing (declared outcome not produced), or untraceable
criteria.sufficiency: An INSPECTED journey trace for every advertised workflow with conforming and failing hops recorded; a workflow whose hops cannot be resolved from source is untraceable, and when untraceable workflows reach half of the advertised set the criterion resolves UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: Every advertised workflow traces end to end with all hops conforming
levels.P75: Every advertised workflow produces its declared outcome, and at least one contains a hop deviating from the declared path or representation without breaking the outcome
levels.P50: No core advertised workflow fails end to end, and at least one non-core advertised workflow fails or at least one workflow is untraceable
levels.P25: At least one core advertised workflow fails end to end, or more than a third of advertised workflows fail
levels.FAIL: More than half of advertised workflows fail end to end

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject advertises capabilities in documentation, specification, or contract surfaces; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject advertises no capabilities, since there is no advertised surface to census
criteria.expected: Every advertised capability is backed by a non-trivial implementation - no stub, placeholder, or unwired path stands behind an advertised capability
criteria.method: Advertised-capability reality check plus shipped-surface completeness census: enumerate advertised capabilities, read each backing code path, and census unimplemented-throw sites, empty public types, constant-success methods, conditionally-compiled or never-called modules, and feature-flagged fallbacks; confirm every candidate by reading the mechanism, its guards, and its callers
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED confirmation for every census candidate behind an advertised capability, with the advertised-capability denominator recorded; a pattern match alone is a candidate, never a finding. UNKNOWN floor: the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when the advertised capabilities cannot be enumerated (no documentation, specification, or contract surface to read) or when some census candidates behind advertised capabilities cannot be confirmed or dismissed by inspection - unless a confirmed stub already exists, which resolves FAIL regardless of census completeness

levels.PASS: The shipped-surface completeness census ran over every advertised capability and confirmed zero stubs, placeholders, or unwired paths behind any advertised capability
levels.FAIL: At least one confirmed stub, placeholder, or unwired path stands behind an advertised capability - a stub behind an advertised capability is a spec violation: the subject advertises a capability it does not deliver, breaking an advertised requirement end to end, so the level is FAIL whether the capability is core or not

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships in-scope production source for the defect-pattern census to run over; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no inspectable source, since the census has no denominator
criteria.expected: The defect-pattern census over in-scope source confirms no defect affecting advertised or core behavior
criteria.method: Run the defect-pattern census across the in-scope source - unimplemented throws, always-false comparisons, boundary inversions, inverted arithmetic, wrong-variable checks, discarded configuration, lifecycle and ordering errors, dead catch branches - and confirm each candidate by reading the mechanism, its guards, and its callers, recording the pattern and the denominator
criteria.sufficiency: Every census candidate confirmed or dismissed by INSPECTED reading of its mechanism, guards, and callers, with the census denominator (candidates raised and candidates confirmed) recorded; the candidate list is not a defect count, and an open confirmed defect means one present and unmitigated in the inspected source. UNKNOWN floor: the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when the defect-pattern census cannot run over the in-scope source, or when fewer than half of raised candidates can be confirmed or dismissed by inspection; a census confirmed over at least half of candidates with an unconfirmed residue supports at most P50, the residue recorded as open candidates, never as defects

levels.PASS: The defect-pattern census is complete over the in-scope source and zero open confirmed defects exist on shipped behavior
levels.P75: The census is complete and at most one open confirmed defect exists, of low severity and off every core advertised workflow
levels.P50: The census is complete with one to three open confirmed defects, none above medium severity and none on a core advertised workflow
levels.P25: An open confirmed defect sits on a core advertised workflow, an open confirmed defect carries high or critical severity, or more than three open confirmed defects exist - and no confirmed defect breaks a mandatory requirement end to end
levels.FAIL: A confirmed defect breaks a mandatory requirement end to end - a shipped behavior the requirement demands cannot complete

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject declares external contracts as committed schemas, spec documents, or checked-in generated contract files; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject declares no external contract artifact
criteria.expected: Every declared external contract element - schema member, spec operation, generated contract surface - is implemented with matching names, types, and shapes
criteria.method: Spec-conformance diff per artifact class: enumerate the declared contract surface and the implemented surface, then diff declared-but-unimplemented elements, implemented-but-undeclared elements, and name or type mismatches
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED declaration and implementation sites for every contract element; generated contracts are checked against their checked-in artifacts, never against prose descriptions. The denominator is the set of elements declared in committed contract artifacts - committed schemas, spec documents, and checked-in generated contract files - and prose counts only where the prose is itself the declared contract. UNKNOWN floor: the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when the declared surface cannot be enumerated because referenced contract artifacts are absent from the tree or external, or when more than half of declared elements lack an inspectable declaration or implementation site; a partially enumerable surface where at least half of declared elements are verified supports at most P50, unverifiable elements recorded as unresolved, never as matches

levels.PASS: Every element declared in committed contract artifacts is matched by an inspected implementation site with equal name, type, and shape, and no declared element is missing
levels.P75: Every declared element is implemented correctly, and implemented-but-undeclared surface exists that the committed contract artifacts do not describe
levels.P50: Declared-but-unimplemented elements or name and type mismatches exist on a third or fewer of the declared contract elements, none on the contract's primary operations
levels.P25: Mismatches or missing elements affect a primary contract operation, or more than a third of the declared contract elements
levels.FAIL: The majority of declared contract elements are missing or mismatched - the committed contract artifacts do not describe the shipped surface

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships source and advertises workflows or externally reachable entry points; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject advertises no workflows, since the coverage denominator is empty
criteria.expected: Advertised workflows and externally reachable entry points are exercised by tests
criteria.method: Verification-coverage map: enumerate dispatch entry points from registration sites and advertised workflows from documentation and the profile, and map each to the tests that name it; reconcile test files against declared include patterns so only tests that can run count
criteria.sufficiency: A test counts only when it names the journey or entry point, asserts on its behavior, and is selected by a declared include pattern; counted test functions without the workflow map are an insufficient substitute; entry points no test references are recorded coverage gaps. UNKNOWN floor: the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when the advertised-workflow enumeration cannot be produced from documentation and profile surfaces, or when test files cannot be reconciled against include patterns for more than half the suite so that which tests can run is undecidable; a coverage map that reconciles all runnable tests but covers only part of the advertised set is a level result, not UNKNOWN, while a map partial on the test side with at least half of workflows resolved supports at most P50

levels.PASS: Every advertised workflow is named by at least one include-pattern-selected test that asserts on its behavior, and at least 90% of enumerated entry points are named by such tests
levels.P75: Every core advertised workflow is named by a runnable asserting test, and at least 75% of advertised workflows and of enumerated entry points are covered
levels.P50: At least half of advertised workflows are named by runnable asserting tests
levels.P25: A runnable suite exists but fewer than half of advertised workflows are named by tests that assert on them
levels.FAIL: No runnable test names any advertised workflow, or no include-pattern-selected suite exists where the subject advertises workflows

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships source and advertises workflows carrying error branches; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject advertises no workflows, since there is no failure-path denominator
criteria.expected: Error branches and failure paths of advertised workflows are exercised by tests
criteria.method: Failure-path index: enumerate the error branches on advertised-workflow paths - rejection, validation failure, and dependency failure paths - and the tests exercising each; count workflows with at least one negative-case test
criteria.sufficiency: A failure-path test must exercise the production error branch; coverage that exercises only a double's canned error is recorded as double-only, not production-path coverage

levels.PASS: Every advertised workflow has at least one test exercising a failure path or negative case
levels.P75: All core advertised workflows have failure-path tests and at least 75% of advertised workflows do
levels.P50: At least half of advertised workflows have failure-path coverage
levels.P25: Fewer than half of advertised workflows have failure-path coverage, and isolated negative tests exist
levels.FAIL: No test exercises a failure path - the suite asserts happy paths only, or no suite exists

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships source where a test suite can exist - a source-bearing subject with no suite resolves FAIL, not NOT_APPLICABLE; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model only when the subject ships no inspectable source
criteria.expected: Tests assert observable behavior rather than construction, constants, or their own doubles
criteria.method: Assertion-depth sample: take a stratified sample of tests across suites, classify each as behavioral (asserts outcomes or state changes), structural (asserts construction, defaults, or schema shape only), or circular (re-asserts a double's fixed output), and record the sample frame
criteria.sufficiency: The recorded sample frame and per-test classification suffice; a test asserting a stub's constant counts as circular, not behavioral; counted test functions alone are an insufficient substitute

levels.PASS: At least 90% of sampled tests are behavioral and no circular test is found
levels.P75: At least 75% of sampled tests are behavioral and no circular test stands on an advertised-workflow path
levels.P50: At least half of sampled tests are behavioral, or circular tests exist only off advertised-workflow paths
levels.P25: Fewer than half of sampled tests are behavioral, or a circular test stands as an advertised workflow's only coverage
levels.FAIL: The sample is dominated by structural or circular tests - the suite evidences construction, not behavior, or no suite exists

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships source where unit tests can exist - a source-bearing subject with no suite resolves FAIL, not NOT_APPLICABLE; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model only when the subject ships no inspectable source
criteria.expected: Units can be tested in isolation - external boundaries are replaced by doubles mapped to real production boundaries
criteria.method: Test-double inventory: list the doubles and fixtures in the suite, map each to the production boundary it replaces, and check whether unit tests instantiate units with injected dependencies or require live external resources
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED wiring between each test double and the production boundary it replaces; a double that replaces no production boundary is recorded, not credited. UNKNOWN floor: the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when the suite's double inventory cannot be mapped to production boundaries for more than half of the external boundaries the tests exercise, because tests or boundary code are uninspectable; a partial map covering at least half of exercised boundaries supports at most P50, the unmapped residue recorded

levels.PASS: Every external boundary exercised by unit tests has a double inspected as wired to the production boundary it replaces, and no unit test requires a live external service, real credential, or non-hermetic resource
levels.P75: Inspected double-to-boundary wiring holds for all core boundaries; unit tests reference real resources only on non-core paths
levels.P50: Doubles inspected as wired to production boundaries exist for the main external boundaries, but several unit tests construct concrete dependencies inline or touch real resources
levels.P25: Fewer than half of exercised external boundaries have doubles wired to them; most unit tests need the wider environment
levels.FAIL: No test doubles exist and every test exercises concrete dependencies end to end, or no test suite exists

criteria.applicability: Applies to the automated change-verification gate of the owning project; NOT_APPLICABLE via census-none when the owning project's automation census resolves none - no pipeline or automation definitions exist for the census to inspect. When the census is signals or external the criterion must be resolved, with external surfaces recorded as Reported evidence
criteria.expected: The automated pipeline runs the test suite on change and a failing result blocks merge or release
criteria.method: Inspect pipeline and workflow definitions: change triggers, test invocation steps, required checks, gates, and branch or release protection configuration
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED pipeline definitions showing the trigger, the test step, and the blocking mechanism; under an external census only in-tree aspects are judged and the external pointer is recorded as Reported evidence; documentation claiming tests run is an insufficient substitute. UNKNOWN floor: the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when the census-visible pipeline definitions cannot be inspected - an external system with no in-tree definitions and an uninspectable pointer; where in-tree definitions exist they are judged directly, and partial definitions showing a trigger and a test step but not the blocking mechanism support at most P50

levels.PASS: Inspected pipeline definitions run the include-pattern-selected test suite on every change event, and failure blocks merge or release per required-check, gate, or protection configuration
levels.P75: The runnable suite runs on change and failure blocks, but blocking covers only a subset of suites or protected branches
levels.P50: Tests run automatically on change but no blocking mechanism is configured - results are informational only
levels.P25: A pipeline exists but the test step cannot gate - it is manual-trigger only, marked continue-on-error, or selects only a small subset of the runnable suite
levels.FAIL: No census-visible pipeline definition contains a test execution step - automation exists but never runs tests

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source organized into areas or units; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no production source
criteria.expected: Each production unit and area has a single coherent responsibility - no catch-all unit spans unrelated domains
criteria.method: Responsibility inventory per the organization model: record the observed responsibility of every production area, census areas or units whose observed responsibilities span unrelated domains, and measure the share of production source they hold
criteria.sufficiency: An observed role is recorded for every inspected production area; a populated area with no identifiable responsibility counts as a catch-all, never a pass

levels.PASS: Zero catch-all units - every inspected production area carries one coherent responsibility
levels.P75: Catch-all units exist only in non-core areas and hold at most 10% of production source
levels.P50: Catch-all units hold more than 10% but at most half of production source, or at least one serves a core advertised workflow
levels.P25: Catch-all units hold more than half of production source, but the majority of areas still carry a coherent responsibility
levels.FAIL: The majority of production areas lack a coherent single responsibility - catch-all structure is the norm

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source with cross-module consumer edges; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no production source or a single undivided unit with no module boundaries to census
criteria.expected: Cross-module dependencies are expressed as abstractions and injected; clients depend on narrow interfaces, not fat ones with unused members
criteria.method: Dependency-edge census: for each cross-boundary consumer edge, record whether the dependency runs through an abstraction (interface, protocol, trait, or abstract type) that is injected, or a concrete low-level type constructed inline; census interfaces whose implementers stub members clients never call
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED edges across module boundaries from the producer-consumer matrix; the existence of an interface is insufficient - the edge must run through the abstraction

levels.PASS: All cross-boundary dependencies between distinct production modules run through abstractions where substitution matters, and no implementer stubs members of a fat interface
levels.P75: Abstractions carry at least 90% of cross-boundary edges; concrete inline construction is confined to leaf utilities and no fat-interface stubs exist
levels.P50: Abstractions carry at least half of cross-boundary edges, or at least one fat interface forces implementers to stub unused members
levels.P25: Fewer than half of cross-boundary edges use abstractions; concrete low-level types are constructed inline as the norm on core paths
levels.FAIL: Cross-boundary dependencies are concrete everywhere substitution is needed - no abstraction isolates a high-level unit from low-level details

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source spanning more than one module; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no production source or a single module with no inter-module edges to census
criteria.expected: Production modules couple minimally through stable contracts - the dependency graph is acyclic and respects the declared layering
criteria.method: Producer-consumer edge census: record module-level dependency edges and their mechanism, detect cycles, edges violating the declared or evident layer direction, and fan-out outliers (a module consuming more than a third of production areas)
criteria.sufficiency: The edge census covers every production module; unresolved dynamic edges are recorded as unresolved, never assumed acyclic

levels.PASS: Zero dependency cycles, zero declared-layer violations, and no fan-out outlier
levels.P75: No cycles and no layer violation on a core path; at most one fan-out outlier or one layer violation in a non-core module
levels.P50: Cycles exist confined to a bounded set of non-core modules, a declared-layer violation exists off core paths, or several fan-out outliers exist
levels.P25: A cycle or layer violation sits on a core advertised path, or cycles span more than a third of production modules
levels.FAIL: The dependency graph is cyclic or directionless across the majority of modules - no layering is discernible

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source with an enumerable responsibility inventory; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no production source
criteria.expected: Each responsibility has one owning implementation - no competing or parallel implementations of the same responsibility exist
criteria.method: From the responsibility inventory, count the responsibilities claimed by two or more production areas (competing ownership) and the duplicated construction or extension logic spread across files
criteria.sufficiency: Competing ownership is recorded under both areas with the overlap noted; naming similarity alone is not duplication - the observed responsibilities must match

levels.PASS: Every production responsibility has exactly one owning implementation
levels.P75: Competing implementations exist for at most one non-core responsibility, with the overlap recorded
levels.P50: Two or more responsibilities have competing implementations, or a core responsibility is implemented in parallel without a recorded rationale
levels.P25: Competing implementations span core areas - parallel subsystems implement the same domains
levels.FAIL: Competing ownership is the norm across major responsibilities - no single source of truth exists for core behavior

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject's codebase is large enough to exhibit recurring structure; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the codebase is too trivial to exhibit recurring structure, per the design-patterns guide's own N/A rule
criteria.expected: Identified design patterns fit the stated context and are applied consistently - no anti-pattern removes the flexibility a pattern exists to provide
criteria.method: Pattern inventory: name each recurring structure by its catalog name, anchor it to a type or file, and judge presence, fitness, consistency, and injectability; census anti-patterns such as hardcoded strategy variants, ad-hoc dispatch beside a declared command abstraction, and inconsistently applied factories
criteria.sufficiency: Every claimed pattern is anchored to inspected code; a pattern is flagged only when its application is inconsistent, redundant, or removes the value it exists to provide - an unusual but fitting pattern is a strength

levels.PASS: Every identified pattern is applied consistently and fits the stated constraints; zero confirmed anti-patterns
levels.P75: Patterns are consistent, with at most one isolated inconsistency or anti-pattern instance on a non-core path
levels.P50: At least one pattern is applied in mixed forms, or a confirmed anti-pattern exists off core paths
levels.P25: A confirmed anti-pattern sits on a core advertised path, or several patterns are inconsistently applied
levels.FAIL: Anti-patterns dominate the recurring structures - the patterns in use remove the flexibility they exist for

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships source in a language ecosystem that supports static analysis, type checking, or formatting tooling; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no source or its stack supports none of these tool classes
criteria.expected: Static analysis, type checking, and formatting are configured with meaningful rule sets for every primary language partition
criteria.method: Inspect linter and analyzer, type-checker, and formatter configuration files per language partition; record declared rules, strictness flags, and exclusions; committed tool output is Reported evidence
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED configuration files naming rules and strictness; configuration is evidence of configuration, not of enforcement or a clean run, and an empty or all-disabled config does not count

levels.PASS: Every primary language partition has linter or analyzer configuration with a non-trivial rule set, formatter configuration, and strict type-checker settings where the ecosystem supports gradual strictness
levels.P75: All three tool classes are configured for the main partition, but the rule set is loose or exclusions are broad, or a minor partition lacks configuration
levels.P50: At least one tool class (lint, type check, or format) is configured meaningfully for the main partition; the others are absent or token
levels.P25: Configuration files exist but enable near-nothing - rules disabled wholesale, strictness off, or configs covering only a minor partition
levels.FAIL: No static analysis, type-check, or formatter configuration exists where the stack supports it

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source containing methods or units; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no inspectable source
criteria.expected: Methods and units are bounded in estimated complexity and size - core logic is not concentrated in very long or deeply nested functions
criteria.method: Estimate cyclomatic complexity per method from source alone (one per method plus one per decision point), census methods above 20, and census extreme size outliers against the project's own distribution
criteria.sufficiency: The census denominator (methods inspected) and the per-method estimates are recorded; estimates are Inferred evidence unless a committed metrics report supplies the values

levels.PASS: No method exceeds an estimated complexity of 20 and no file is an extreme size outlier against the project's own distribution
levels.P75: Above-threshold methods are at most 2% of inspected methods and confined to non-core paths
levels.P50: Above-threshold methods are at most 10% of inspected methods, including isolated core units
levels.P25: More than 10% of inspected methods exceed the threshold, or the largest units concentrate the majority of core logic in deeply nested functions
levels.FAIL: Extreme complexity is the norm in core areas - most core methods exceed the threshold

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source spanning multiple files; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no production source. Detection is decidable without tooling - the census is read-through structural comparison, not an external scan
criteria.expected: Logic is shared rather than repeated - no near-duplicate blocks span files and no divergent implementations serve one function
criteria.method: Token-based or structural near-duplicate scan across production files, plus a divergent-implementation census (two libraries or APIs serving one function); record each cluster's files and extent
criteria.sufficiency: Each candidate cluster is confirmed by structural comparison - the same operation sequence under renamed identifiers counts; suspected similarity without inspection does not. Duplication detection is decidable from inspection alone: the census compares same-responsibility units across files by read-through, and no external scan tool is required - a committed tool report is Reported evidence only, never a substitute. UNKNOWN floor: the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when more than half of production source is uninspectable, for example files missing or generated bundles inseparable from hand-written code; inspection of at least half the source supports at most P50, with uninspected regions recorded, never counted clean

levels.PASS: The read-through census confirms no near-duplicate cluster spans files and no divergent implementations serve one function
levels.P75: Confirmed duplication is confined to a single bounded cluster under 5% of production source, or one divergent pair confined to a non-core concern
levels.P50: Confirmed duplication covers 5-15% of production source, or a divergent pair serves a core-adjacent function
levels.P25: Confirmed duplication covers more than 15% of production source or spans core logic
levels.FAIL: Duplication is systematic - repeated logic and parallel implementations are the dominant structure

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source or dependency manifests; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no production source
criteria.expected: The tree contains no unreachable or unused code - no dead helpers or exports, no wholly commented-out source files, no unused manifest dependencies
criteria.method: Dead-code census: call-site search for exported helpers and modules no caller reaches, commented-out share per file and per project, unused manifest or lockfile entries by import-or-reference verdict, and unreachable branches
criteria.sufficiency: Reachability is confirmed by call-site search with module inclusion verified - an unused verdict needs the import-or-reference check, not name absence; unused-dependency findings coordinate with the dependency assessment, which owns the advisory view

levels.PASS: Zero confirmed dead code: no unreachable helpers or exports, no wholly commented-out source files, commented-out share under 1% of production lines, and no unused manifest entry
levels.P75: Confirmed dead code is confined to a bounded set off core paths - commented-out share under 5%, isolated unused exports or manifest entries
levels.P50: Commented-out share is at least 5% of production lines, or confirmed dead modules or helpers sit on supported paths, or several manifest entries are unused
levels.P25: Confirmed dead code spans core areas - unreachable modules or large commented-out regions sit on advertised paths
levels.FAIL: Dead and commented-out code is pervasive - the tree cannot be trusted to reflect what executes

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source in a language with exception or error-handler constructs; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no source or its stack has no handler construct to census
criteria.expected: Error paths are handled, not silently discarded - no empty catch blocks, no catch-all swallow, no unreachable error handling
criteria.method: Catch-block census: count handlers that discard an error without handling, logging, or propagating; overly broad catch-alls that collapse distinct error families into silence; and handlers for exception types the guarded block cannot raise
criteria.sufficiency: Each candidate is confirmed by reading the handler body and the guarded block - a handler that logs and rethrows is not a discard; dead-catch candidates confirmed under the defect census count there once, not again here. The census denominator is every catch or error-handler site in production source, recorded as N inspected handlers. UNKNOWN floor: the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when more than half of handler sites cannot be inspected because source is unavailable or unparseable; inspection of at least half the handler set supports at most P50, uninspected sites recorded

levels.PASS: The census covers every catch or error-handler site in production source and confirms zero silent discards and zero dead catch branches
levels.P75: At most two confirmed silent discards among all inspected handlers, all on non-core auxiliary paths
levels.P50: Three or more confirmed silent discards all confined to non-core auxiliary paths, or any confirmed silent discard or overly broad catch-all on a supported non-core path - none on core advertised paths or the error-handling boundary
levels.P25: A confirmed silent discard or catch-all swallow sits on a core advertised path or on the error-handling boundary
levels.FAIL: Silent error discarding is the norm - the majority of inspected handlers discard failures without surfacing them

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source with identifier declarations to classify; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no inspectable source
criteria.expected: One convention dominates identifier casing, prefix, and suffix shapes per language partition and identifier kind
criteria.method: Identifier-shape census per partition and kind with recorded declaration-shaped patterns; classify each declaration by shape family, compute the dominant-shape share with denominators, and exclude generated, vendored, and contract-forced names
criteria.sufficiency: Census rows record the exact pattern and denominator (n/N and %) per partition and kind, with the winning convention tier named; partitions below the minimum share get a note, not a profile; a dominant share under 75% is a split, not a convention

levels.PASS: Dominant-shape share is at least 90% for every identifier kind in every material partition and the convention resolves to a named tier
levels.P75: At least 90% dominant for all kinds in the main partitions; kinds or minor partitions in the 75-90% band carry a bounded outlier list
levels.P50: The dominant shape in a main partition sits in the 75-90% band - drift with a clear leader
levels.P25: A main partition stays at or above 75% dominant but several identifier kinds fall below 75% - the split is confined to part of the surface
levels.FAIL: No identifier kind in a main partition reaches 75% dominant share, or distinct style families mix inside one partition

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source with identifiers or comments; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no inspectable source
criteria.expected: One concept carries one word across the codebase; initialism casing is uniform; identifiers and comments use a single human language
criteria.method: Vocabulary census: enumerate concept-term pairs (for example get/fetch/load, cfg/conf/config, remove/delete, singular/plural variants) and initialism casings; count concepts spelled more than one way and mixed-language identifiers or comments
criteria.sufficiency: Concept-term pairs are counted mechanically per partition with denominators; a term a framework mandates is excluded per the ecosystem anti-pattern rules

levels.PASS: Every enumerated concept uses a single term, initialism casing is uniform, and no mixed human languages appear in identifiers or comments
levels.P75: Single-term conformance holds on exported surfaces, with at most isolated vocabulary variants internally
levels.P50: Several concepts carry competing terms or initialism casing varies, confined to internal identifiers
levels.P25: Competing vocabulary or mixed languages reach exported identifiers, comments, or API surfaces
levels.FAIL: No stable vocabulary exists - the same concept is spelled several ways as the norm across the surface

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source with identifiers; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no inspectable source
criteria.expected: Identifiers state responsibility honestly - no misleading names, noise names at wide scope, missing units, ad-hoc abbreviations, or typo collisions
criteria.method: Stratified naming-quality sample over every top-level module, the public API surface, the largest and most-churned files, and the entry points, capped by the sample rule; classify each heuristic hit with file:line and record the sample frame
criteria.sufficiency: Every hit carries file:line and the heuristic it violates, with the sample frame recorded; naming-quality findings carry confidence MEDIUM or lower; ecosystem-idiomatic short names are excluded per the anti-pattern list

levels.PASS: No misleading names on any surface, and noise-name or missing-unit hits are absent from the exported and config surface with internal hits under 5% of sampled identifiers
levels.P75: Naming-quality hits are confined to internal identifiers - none on the public API, config keys, or security-relevant paths
levels.P50: Misleading or noise names appear on internal surfaces above 5% of the sample, or isolated misleading names reach exported surfaces
levels.P25: Misleading names sit on the public API or security-relevant paths, or more than 25% of identifiers in a core partition fail the heuristics
levels.FAIL: Misleading naming is pervasive across the exported surface - names contradict behavior on core paths

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships production source; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject ships no inspectable source
criteria.expected: Source is readable at inspection - comments explain intent where non-obvious, markers are bounded, and no extreme cognitive-load outliers exist
criteria.method: Sample comments for stale or contradictory content, census TODO, FIXME, and HACK markers per 1000 production lines, count magic numbers versus named constants, and census cognitive-load outliers (units beyond roughly three times the project's own 90th percentile on nesting, length, or parameter count)
criteria.sufficiency: The marker census records its counting rule; cognitive-load outliers use the project's own distribution, never fixed absolute numbers; commented-out code is scored under the dead-code criterion, not here

levels.PASS: Marker density under 1 per 1000 production lines, no stale or contradictory comment in the sample, and no cognitive-load outlier
levels.P75: Marker density under 5 per 1000 lines, with isolated stale comments or one outlier on a non-core unit
levels.P50: Marker density 5-15 per 1000 lines, or several cognitive-load outliers including a core unit
levels.P25: Marker density above 15 per 1000 lines, contradictory comments on core paths, or extreme outliers concentrating core logic
levels.FAIL: Markers, stale comments, and extreme outliers are pervasive - core source resists inspection

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject declares style or naming rules in tooling configuration or documents; NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model when the subject declares no style or naming rules, since the criterion has nothing to check
criteria.expected: Where style or naming rules are declared in tooling or documents, the code conforms and suppressions are sparse
criteria.method: Compare declared style rules (formatter, naming, and lint-style settings) against sampled code on indentation, line length, brace style, import order, and end-of-line, and count naming or style rule suppressions per partition
criteria.sufficiency: Declared rules are inspected from configuration; drift requires sampled code contradicting a declared rule - a canonical formatter with no config file is not a defect; the criterion is NOT_APPLICABLE when the subject declares no style or naming rules

levels.PASS: Sampled code conforms to every declared style rule and suppression density is near zero per partition
levels.P75: Conformance holds with isolated drift or sparse suppressions confined to one partition
levels.P50: Declared rules are contradicted on one axis, for example line length or import order, or suppression density is moderate
levels.P25: Declared rules are contradicted on several axes, or suppressions are dense enough to suspend the convention in a partition
levels.FAIL: Declared conventions are systematically contradicted - the configuration describes code that does not exist

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Production code in every language partition uses the language's standard constructs and idioms rather than patterns ported from another language
criteria.method: Foreign-idiom census per partition against the resolved stack baseline: flag constructs that transcribe another language's model onto this stack (foreign error-handling shapes, ported control patterns, non-native constructs where the language offers a standard one); classify each site against the baseline, project-declared rules winning over ecosystem defaults
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED census over every production partition; a partition whose stack cannot be identified resolves UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: The foreign-idiom census records zero confirmed sites in every partition
levels.P75: Confirmed foreign-idiom sites appear in at most 2 files across all partitions, none on an entry-point or shared-library path
levels.P50: Confirmed foreign-idiom sites appear in more than 2 files, or at least one sits on an entry-point or shared-library path, while native idioms remain dominant in every partition
levels.FAIL: Ported idioms are the dominant pattern in a partition - the code reads as a transcription of a different stack

criteria.applicability: Applies to every partition using a detectable framework; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) for a stdlib-only subject exercising no framework - a framework present but unidentifiable resolves UNKNOWN, never N/A
criteria.expected: Detected frameworks are used through their prescribed structure, lifecycle, data flow, and extension points; the framework's mechanisms are not bypassed or reimplemented
criteria.method: Per detected framework, census how each exercised capability is wired: registration and routing sites, lifecycle hooks, dependency-injection and configuration mechanisms, error-handling hooks; count confirmed bypass sites where code routes around the framework mechanism or reimplements it
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED wiring trace for every exercised framework capability; framework identity is read from manifests and registration sites

levels.PASS: Every exercised framework capability is wired through its documented extension point and the bypass census records zero confirmed sites
levels.P75: At most 2 confirmed bypass sites, none touching a core mechanism (routing, lifecycle, dependency injection, error handling)
levels.P50: More than 2 confirmed bypass sites, or one core mechanism partially bypassed while other uses of it conform
levels.FAIL: A core framework mechanism is bypassed or reimplemented on the main execution path, or the framework is used as a shell while its prescribed structure is ignored

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Problems the stack's established libraries already solve use those libraries; every hand-rolled equivalent carries a recorded justification
criteria.method: Hand-rolled-implementation census: locate each site where production code reimplements a problem an established ecosystem library solves at the installed stack version - 'established' means the library is named in the stack digest's recommended set or the ecosystem's canonical guidance for that version; the census denominator is only problems with such library coverage, a custom implementation addressing a problem no established library covers stays out of the count; per counted site record whether a justification is committed in the tree (code comment, design document, manifest note, or decision record naming the reason) - an auditor-inferred rationale is not a justification; two-libraries-for-one-function is excluded, it belongs to the code-quality duplication census
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED sites plus a committed justification or its recorded absence per site; a site counts as a defect only when both conditions hold - an established library covers the problem at the installed stack version and no justification is committed in the tree; a site whose library coverage cannot be established is recorded unresolved, and the criterion resolves UNKNOWN only when every candidate site is unresolved

levels.PASS: Zero defect sites: every hand-rolled implementation either addresses a problem no established library covers at the installed version or carries a committed justification
levels.P75: Exactly 1 defect site, off the security and data-integrity paths
levels.P50: 2 or more defect sites, or one defect site on a data path
levels.FAIL: A defect site reimplementing a security-relevant solved problem (cryptography, authentication, wire protocol), or unjustified reimplementation is the systematic pattern across a capability area

criteria.applicability: Applies to every subject carrying a code partition with a resolvable stack; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when no stack floor can exist at all, for example a document-only subject
criteria.expected: The code is current with its declared toolchain floor: no calls to APIs the stack flags as deprecated or discouraged for the installed version, and constructs use the patterns the declared version offers rather than superseded pre-floor idioms
criteria.method: Resolve the declared toolchain floor from each partition's manifest; census call sites hitting APIs the stack's canonical guidance or deprecation metadata flags for that version, plus superseded-idiom sites named in the stack's digest
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED census against a resolvable floor and a consulted baseline; a partition whose floor and baseline cannot both be resolved resolves UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: Zero deprecated-API call sites and zero superseded-idiom sites against the declared floor
levels.P75: 1-2 confirmed sites combined
levels.P50: 3 or more confirmed sites combined, below the systematic threshold
levels.FAIL: Deprecated or superseded constructs are systematic in a capability area (more than half of its files carry one), or a removed-in-a-later-major API sits on the main execution path

criteria.applicability: Applies to every production-code partition; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when the subject carries no production code
criteria.expected: Anti-patterns the detected stack's canonical guidance names as convention defects are absent from production code
criteria.method: For each partition, apply the convention-class checkable constraints in the matching references/stacks/ digest, or the project-declared convention baseline where one exists; a detected anti-pattern is a code location confirmed against a named constraint in that baseline - a suspicion backed by no named constraint is recorded as an observation and never enters the count; constraints already bound to another dimension (security sinks, dead code, structure placement, test shapes) are excluded so no property is counted twice
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED census against the partition's digest or declared baseline; a partition whose stack has no digest entry and no project-declared baseline resolves UNKNOWN; a partition the census cannot complete over is recorded unresolved and the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when every partition is unresolved

levels.PASS: Zero confirmed sites across all partitions - every checked location conforms to a named convention-class constraint of the resolved baseline
levels.P50: 1-3 confirmed sites, none embedded in a construct other code builds on (a shared helper, base type, middleware, or framework registration consumed by other modules)
levels.FAIL: 4 or more confirmed sites, or at least one confirmed site embedded in a shared mechanism other modules consume

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Direct dependencies declare resolvable version constraints and the resolved set is locked for reproducible builds; the lockfile agrees with the manifests in both directions
criteria.method: Per manifest, classify each direct declaration as exact pin, bounded range, or unpinned/floating; check lockfile presence and manifest-lockfile drift both directions (declared entry missing from lockfile, locked component with no declared path); count vendored components carrying a recorded version
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED read of every manifest and lockfile per references/dependency-manifests.md; a published library whose registry resolves declared ranges at install time counts declared ranges as conforming and does not require a lockfile

levels.PASS: Every direct dependency carries an exact pin or bounded constraint, and either a lockfile resolves the full declared set with zero drift entries or the component is a published library relying on registry resolution
levels.P75: Lockfile present and consistent, but 1-2 direct dependencies carry loose constraints (unbounded range or floating tag)
levels.P50: Manifest and lockfile both present but drifted, or more than 2 direct dependencies unpinned while a lockfile exists
levels.P25: No lockfile for a deployable product while manifests declare ranges, so the resolved set is undetermined
levels.FAIL: Direct dependencies carry no version constraints at all, or third-party imports exist with no manifest declaring them

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Every resolved component carries an established advisory state from the five-state vocabulary, and no unaddressed KNOWN_APPLICABLE advisory exists in the resolved set
criteria.method: Per resolved component, assign an Advisory state per references/evidence-schema.md by source precedence: a recorded scan or advisory artifact decides KNOWN_* and NONE_IDENTIFIED_BY_RECORDED_SCAN, an inspected mitigation or disabling control decides KNOWN_MITIGATED or KNOWN_NOT_APPLICABLE, and no consulted source renders NOT_CHECKED; record suppressions with rationale, owner, and expiry
criteria.sufficiency: Advisory status requires a recorded scan or advisory artifact covering the component. Under source-only with no committed scan output every component is NOT_CHECKED and the criterion resolves UNKNOWN; a policy file or scanner configuration is intent, never a result

levels.PASS: A recorded scan covering the resolved dependency set reports NONE_IDENTIFIED_BY_RECORDED_SCAN for every component, or every listed advisory carries KNOWN_MITIGATED or KNOWN_NOT_APPLICABLE with its deciding evidence named
levels.P50: A recorded scan exists but its database revision predates the manifest revision or it covers only part of the resolved set, or advisories are listed with an unverified applicability verdict
levels.FAIL: Recorded evidence establishes a KNOWN_APPLICABLE advisory with no mitigation, no suppression carrying rationale, owner and expiry, and no disabling evidence

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: The third-party component set is enumerable for the audited revision: manifests and lockfiles are present and readable, or a machine-readable SBOM tied to the revision or release exists
criteria.method: Run the per-ecosystem readers in references/dependency-manifests.md over every partition importing third-party code; 'readable' means the reader parses the file without error - an unparseable manifest counts as unreadable, not as absent; count readable versus unreadable or absent manifests and lockfiles; check for a committed SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX), recording its schema, generator, and basis (source or shipped artifact) when present
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED manifests and lockfiles producing the full component list, or an INSPECTED committed SBOM; an SBOM for source input does not prove shipped-artifact contents and is recorded as such; the criterion resolves UNKNOWN only when the audit cannot determine which partitions carry third-party imports at all - a readable import census with missing manifests is FAIL, never UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: The full component set is enumerable from committed evidence: a readable manifest covers every partition importing third-party code, every present lockfile parses and agrees with its manifest, and every vendored component carries a recorded version - or a committed SBOM covering the dependency set exists
levels.P75: The inventory is derivable but up to 2 vendored or optional components lack recorded versions and no committed SBOM exists
levels.P50: The inventory is only partially enumerable: the lockfile is absent for a deployable product whose manifest declares ranges, more than 2 components lack recorded versions, or a manifest is absent or unreadable for a partition that imports third-party code
levels.FAIL: The third-party set is not enumerable: no manifest, lockfile, vendored metadata, or SBOM exists while production code imports third-party components

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Every third-party import, load, or link in source resolves to a manifest-declared dependency or a recorded vendored component; no phantom dependencies
criteria.method: Import and load census per partition against the declared and vendored component sets; each third-party import gets a DECLARED or PHANTOM verdict; language runtime and standard-library imports are excluded
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED import census per partition with denominators; the reverse direction (declared-but-unused entries) is measured by the code-quality dead-code criterion and excluded here

levels.PASS: Zero phantom imports across all partitions
levels.P75: 1-2 phantom imports, all confined to test, tooling, or example code
levels.P50: Phantom imports exist in production code but stay inside one non-core module
levels.FAIL: Phantom imports span 2 or more production areas or sit on a core execution path

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Every dependency manifest carries the metadata its stack's manifest spec names: a machine-readable license or license-file field, the toolchain floor field, and repository and description fields where the spec requires them
criteria.method: Per manifest, check the metadata fields the stack's manifest specification names, split into required fields (the machine-readable license or license-file field and the toolchain floor field) and secondary fields (repository, description, and other informational spec fields); a field counts only where the manifest format defines it - a format carrying no license field is judged on the fields it defines; count missing fields by class
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED manifest reads; the license-obligation assessment itself belongs to the licensing review - this criterion measures only field presence; an absent manifest for a dependency-carrying component is already a FAIL finding and an unreadable manifest counts the fields its format defines as missing, so UNKNOWN applies only when whether any manifest exists cannot be determined

levels.PASS: Every manifest carries all fields its stack spec names, required and secondary, across the fields its format defines
levels.P50: Only secondary fields (repository, description, or other informational spec fields) are missing while the license field and the toolchain floor are declared wherever the format defines them
levels.FAIL: The license field or the toolchain floor is missing on a manifest whose format defines it, or no manifest exists for a component carrying dependencies

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Every explicitly declared target - runtime, framework, language version, OS target, or long-lived platform version - carries an established vendor support status
criteria.method: Census declared targets across manifests and platform documents; per target resolve its version signal from committed evidence (manifest pin or floor, vendored component metadata, release-note or vendored-documentation version record, committed lifecycle-check record) and assign supported, EOL, or EOL-via-parent-product against the vendor's lifecycle policy, citing the page, committed check, or dated corpus verdict that establishes the status
criteria.sufficiency: Per declared target, grade against the vendor's lifecycle policy wherever a resolvable version signal exists anywhere in the tree; UNKNOWN applies only to a declared target carrying no version or lifecycle signal at all, and the criterion resolves UNKNOWN only when every declared target is unsignalled - a stale-looking but resolvable signal grades at the level its established status supports, never UNKNOWN-by-default; a subject declaring no targets resolves PASS with the vacuity recorded

levels.PASS: Every declared target carries a resolvable version signal, and the consulted lifecycle evidence establishes supported status for all of them
levels.P50: Consulted lifecycle evidence establishes at least one declared target as superseded or EOL-via-parent-product inside a vendor support window, or establishes a target as EOL where a recorded acceptance or migration plan exists in the tree
levels.FAIL: Consulted lifecycle evidence establishes a declared target as EOL and the tree carries no recorded acceptance or migration plan for it

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Technical debt is visible and bounded: explicit debt markers are tracked, and files stay within the resolved baseline's size bound so module growth does not hide responsibilities
criteria.method: Census untracked debt markers (TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX without an issue or owner reference) per production source file; census files beyond the resolved baseline's size-signal bound (500 lines where the baseline is silent); compute both shares over production file count
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED census over all production files with denominators; duplication and dead code are measured by code-quality criteria and excluded here

levels.PASS: Untracked markers appear in at most 2% of production files and at most 1 file exceeds the size bound
levels.P75: Untracked markers appear in at most 5% of production files and at most 5% exceed the size bound
levels.P50: Untracked markers appear in at most 15% of production files and at most 15% exceed the size bound
levels.P25: Untracked markers appear in at most 33% of production files and at most 33% exceed the size bound
levels.FAIL: More than 33% of production files carry untracked markers or exceed the size bound, or core logic concentrates in files beyond 3 times the bound

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Entry documentation explains purpose, setup, and usage; an onboarding path is documented; public interfaces carry documentation
criteria.method: Census the committed documentation surface: presence and completeness of the README or equivalent (purpose, setup, and usage each present as committed content), presence of a documented build-and-run path, and the share of the public-interface surface carrying committed documentation; 'documented' here means committed content exists - whether that content is current or correct is MNT-DOCSYNC's verdict and never lowers a presence verdict in this criterion
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED documents; this criterion measures presence and coverage - whether the documented build and run commands actually resolve is measured by the deployability run-path criterion and doc-code agreement by MNT-DOCSYNC; UNKNOWN applies only when the documentation surface itself cannot be enumerated

levels.PASS: Committed entry documentation covers purpose, setup, and usage, a build-and-run path is documented in the tree, and at least 90% of the public-interface surface carries committed documentation
levels.P75: Committed entry documentation covers purpose, setup, and usage and interface documentation covers 50-90% of the public surface
levels.P50: A committed entry document exists but omits setup or usage, or interface documentation covers less than 50% of the public surface
levels.P25: Only a token entry document is committed (it names the project without a usable setup path)
levels.FAIL: No committed documentation exists where the system's scale clearly requires it: no entry document, or no setup path is documented anywhere

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Documentation agrees with the code: documented figures reproduce, documented commands, options, environment variables, config keys, and file paths resolve to the implemented surface, embedded code excerpts match, and same-named documents do not diverge
criteria.method: Documented-claim verification: recalculate every quantitative claim against the measured repository, diff every documented command, option, env var, key, and path against the implemented surface, classify embedded code blocks and diff current-implementation excerpts, and diff duplicate documents; count findings; the build/run/deploy path itself is censused by the deployability run-path criterion and excluded here
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED verification over the full documented surface; a documented-but-unimplemented item and an implemented-but-undocumented surface both count as drift findings

levels.PASS: Zero drift findings: every checked figure reproduces and every documented item resolves
levels.P75: 1-2 drift findings, none on a documented onboarding or usage path
levels.P50: 3-5 drift findings, or 1 drift finding on a documented usage path
levels.P25: More than 5 drift findings, or divergent duplicate documents on a normative surface
levels.FAIL: Documentation systematically contradicts the code: the documented surface describes a different system than the implemented one

criteria.applicability: Applies to every subject whose scale produces significant, hard-to-reverse decisions; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) for a trivial system where no decision rises to that level
criteria.expected: Significant, hard-to-reverse decisions are recorded with context and consequences, and recorded decisions match the implemented system
criteria.method: Build the significant-decision census for the subject (data store, framework choice, state management model, key algorithm weightings, authentication model, and any equivalent choices); mark each RECORDED or MISSING against a decisions directory or equivalent records; diff recorded decisions against the implemented system for staleness
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED decision records matched to code-embodied decisions; a decision documented only in prose counts as RECORDED when it carries context and consequences

levels.PASS: Every significant decision in the census is RECORDED and current
levels.P75: At most 25% of censused significant decisions are MISSING or stale
levels.P50: 26-50% of censused significant decisions are MISSING, or a recorded decision contradicts the implemented system
levels.P25: More than 50% of censused significant decisions are MISSING
levels.FAIL: No decision is recorded for a system carrying clearly significant, hard-to-reverse choices

criteria.applicability: Applies to every delivery model carrying a governed-path requirement; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) where the delivery model does not - a documented prototype or local-only delivery
criteria.expected: A governed change path exists: change requests and implementation plans pair by a shared identifier, executed changes carry outcome records, a review path is evidenced, changes trace to requirements or work items, a proportionality threshold exempts small fixes, and runtime-selectable behavior can be toggled without redeploy
criteria.method: Census change records for request-plan pairing share, closed-out share, and trace links; verify review-path artifacts (review rules, pull-request templates, code-ownership files); check for a recorded proportionality threshold and for a feature-flag mechanism where the product ships runtime-selectable behavior
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED records and review-path artifacts; unrecorded governance practice is a gap, not a pass - a documented manual process counts as governance only for what it documents

levels.PASS: A review path is evidenced, at least 90% of executed change records are paired and closed out, changes trace to requirements or work items, a proportionality threshold is recorded, and a flag mechanism exists where runtime-selectable behavior ships
levels.P75: A review path is evidenced and at least 70% of executed change records are paired and closed out
levels.P50: A review path or change records exist but pairing and traceability cover less than 70%, or no proportionality record exists
levels.P25: Only fragments exist: a review-path artifact without change records, or change records without any evidenced review path
levels.FAIL: No change control where it is clearly required: no review path, no change records, and risky runtime-selectable behavior ships with no toggle

criteria.applicability: Applies whenever VCS history is in scope; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (history-out-of-scope) when history is absent or out of scope
criteria.expected: Manifest versions advance over the observed history and releases carry tags; a long commit window under a static version with no tags is a release-discipline gap
criteria.method: Over the in-scope history window, compare the manifest-declared version field's committed value across successive release points - the yardstick is the value committed in the manifest, not a changelog entry, tag annotation, or other version claim; count release tags (VCS tags on commits in the window carrying a release-identifier shape, such as a version-shaped or v-prefixed name) against the window's release records; classify windows carrying many commits under a static manifest version and no tags
criteria.sufficiency: Requires VCS history in scope; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (history-out-of-scope) when history is absent or out of scope; resolves UNKNOWN when history is in scope but the manifest version field's history or the tag set cannot be read

levels.PASS: The committed manifest version differs across at least two successive release points and every release in the window carries a VCS tag
levels.P50: The manifest version advances but at least one release in the window is untagged, or release tags exist while the committed manifest version stays static across them
levels.FAIL: A window spanning at least 50 commits or multiple release points sits under a static manifest version with zero release tags, making every build indistinguishable

criteria.applicability: Applies to every subject carrying a populated source tree; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when the subject carries no tree to organize - a populated area with no identifiable responsibility is a finding, never a skip
criteria.expected: A single coherent organizational principle is applied consistently: every populated production area has an identifiable responsibility, no catch-all directory mixes unrelated responsibilities, and no competing organizational models coexist without a recorded rationale
criteria.method: Build the organization model and responsibility inventory per references/organization-model.md; per area record declared versus observed role; census areas whose observed responsibilities span unrelated domains (catch-all), populated areas with no identifiable responsibility, and adjacent areas organized on different principles without a recorded rationale
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED organization model and responsibility inventory covering every populated area; responsibility duplication across areas is measured by the design-soundness criterion and excluded here

levels.PASS: Every populated production area maps to an identifiable responsibility; zero catch-all areas and zero unexplained competing organizational models
levels.P75: Exactly 1 catch-all area or 1 unexplained competing model, outside the core production areas
levels.P50: 2-3 findings across catch-all areas, competing models, or unidentifiable areas, or 1 such finding in a core area
levels.P25: 4 or more such findings
levels.FAIL: No discernible organizational principle: responsibilities cannot be attributed to areas

criteria.applicability: Applies to every subject carrying a source tree with directories and files to name; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when the subject carries no source tree
criteria.expected: Directory and file names follow the resolved baseline: full-word directory discipline, consistent singular-versus-plural usage, file casing per stack, test-file naming parity, and directory-to-namespace alignment
criteria.method: Resolve the naming baseline per partition (project-declared rules, then the corpus matrices, then authoritative sources, then observed dominant convention); census directory names and source and test file names against it; record the conformance share per partition with denominators, classified by convention tier
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED census per partition; in-code identifier naming is measured by the code-style criteria and excluded here; only unexplained deviations count at the established tier

levels.PASS: At least 95% directory and file-name conformance in every partition and zero required-tier deviations
levels.P75: At least 90% conformance in every partition and zero required-tier deviations
levels.P50: At least 75% conformance in every partition, or required-tier deviations confined to one partition
levels.P25: Less than 75% conformance in a partition, or required-tier deviations in 2 or more partitions
levels.FAIL: No dominant naming convention is measurable in a partition (dominant share below 50%)

criteria.applicability: Applies to every subject carrying source code; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when the subject carries no source files
criteria.expected: Declarations divide across files per the language's idiom: one public top-level type per file where the stack prescribes it, cohesive multi-symbol modules where it does not, and abstractions and implementations separated per the stack's convention
criteria.method: Per partition, census files against the stack's code-division rule: count multi-public-type files in one-type-per-file stacks, one-class-per-file fragmentation in module-cohesion stacks, and abstraction-implementation co-location or separation per the matrix; a declared project convention overrides the ecosystem default
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED census over every production partition; N/A when the subject carries no source code

levels.PASS: Zero code-division violations in every partition
levels.P75: 1-2 violating files, none holding a public or shared abstraction
levels.P50: 3 or more violating files, or a violating file holding a public or shared abstraction
levels.P25: More than 10% of production files in a partition violate the division rule
levels.FAIL: Division fights the language's loading or discoverability model at scale: most files in a one-type-per-file stack bundle multiple public types

criteria.applicability: Applies to every subject carrying a file tree to census; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when the subject carries no tree (for example a single-file artifact)
criteria.expected: Source, test, configuration, documentation, and generated classes are separated; supporting artifacts (configuration, build files, CI definitions, scripts, fixtures, migrations) sit where tooling and convention expect them; the baseline files the component role prescribes are present
criteria.method: Tree census per component: verify class separation, placement of each supporting-artifact class against the build and deployment workflow, presence of expected baseline files (README, LICENSE, and other files the component role prescribes), and generated output outside source roots
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED tree census; lockfile presence is measured by DEP-PIN and excluded from the baseline-file check

levels.PASS: All classes are separated per role, every supporting artifact sits where tooling expects, and zero expected baseline files are missing
levels.P75: 1-2 misplaced artifacts or 1 missing expected baseline file
levels.P50: 3 or more misplaced findings, generated output under source roots, or 2 or more missing baseline files
levels.FAIL: No usable separation: tests, generated output, or configuration are intermixed through production roots

criteria.applicability: Applies to every subject carrying source files governed by manifests, indexes, or build definitions; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when the subject carries no source files or no declaring surface
criteria.expected: Every source file on disk is reachable through the component's manifest, index file, build definition, or package declaration, and every declared item exists on disk
criteria.method: Diff the on-disk source file set against manifests, index files, build definitions, and package declarations per component; count orphan files (on disk, unreachable) and phantom declarations (declared, absent on disk)
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED file set and declaration reads; generated directories excluded once recorded as generated in the responsibility inventory

levels.PASS: Zero orphan files and zero phantom declarations
levels.P50: Orphans and phantoms total at most 2, confined outside core production areas
levels.FAIL: Orphaned production files exist that no build or index path reaches, declared components are absent on disk, or more than 2 drift items

criteria.applicability: Applies to every component the delivery model ships as a buildable artifact; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when the subject ships no buildable artifact
criteria.expected: An in-tree build definition produces every deliverable: manifests, build scripts, or container builds are present and internally consistent, and declared toolchain floors and builder image versions satisfy every language feature and dependency minimum the code uses
criteria.method: Census build definitions per deployable component - a build definition is a committed file a named build tool consumes to produce a deliverable (build manifest, build script, Makefile, Dockerfile, or CI build job); 'consistent' means every declared toolchain floor, builder and base image tag, and documented prerequisite equals or exceeds the minimum version each used language feature, each used API, and each declared dependency requires; record each mismatch as a named triple - the used feature or requirement, its minimum-version evidence, and the declared version that predates it - and record any pair of definitions for one component declaring contradictory floors
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED definitions; this criterion measures build-definition consistency, not a completed build - a 'builds successfully' claim requires a recorded build artifact per the Claim Sufficiency deployability row, and a Dockerfile being present is not such proof; a feature-versus-version comparison whose required minimum cannot be established is recorded unresolved, and the criterion resolves UNKNOWN only when every required comparison is unresolved or which components are deployable cannot be determined

levels.PASS: A committed build definition covers every deployable component and zero consistency defects are found
levels.P75: Definitions cover all components with 1-2 inconsistencies that contradict no used feature or dependency minimum
levels.P50: A used feature or dependency minimum postdates a declared floor or builder/base image version (a source-raised build defect), or 1 deployable component lacks a build definition
levels.FAIL: No build definition exists for a component the delivery model must ship, or two definitions for one component declare contradictory floors so no single build path exists

criteria.applicability: Applies when the product carries a runtime configuration surface; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) for a fixed-behavior product with no runtime configuration surface
criteria.expected: Runtime configuration is declared, externalized per environment, and validated: every consumed key is declared in a schema, example, or document, required keys fail fast when missing or invalid, and every injected flag is actually consulted
criteria.method: Census every configuration key a code path reads at runtime against keys declared in a schema, example file, manifest, or committed document - 'consumed' means a code path reads the key or binds it to a typed structure, and 'consulted' means the read value branches or parameterizes behavior, so an injected-but-unconsulted flag is a declared or wired setting with no read path; check startup validation - observable when a schema, binding layer, or explicit startup check rejects a missing or invalid required key before the service path runs; check environment-specific values are externalized rather than hardcoded in source
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED config surface and consumption trace; N/A when the product carries no runtime configuration surface; a key whose consumption cannot be traced to a read path is recorded unresolved rather than auto-declared, and the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when no consumed key can be traced or whether a runtime configuration surface exists cannot be determined

levels.PASS: Every consumed key is declared, every required key is rejected fail-fast by a schema, binding layer, or explicit startup check, environment values are externalized, and zero injected-but-unconsulted flags exist
levels.P75: At most 2 consumed-but-undeclared keys, or at most 2 settings accepting silent defaults where the surface declares validation
levels.P50: More than 2 consumed-but-undeclared keys, required settings broadly accept silent defaults, or a declared or injected setting exists with no read path
levels.FAIL: Required configuration is neither declared nor validated in code: environment-specific values are hardcoded in source, or the product cannot start from declared configuration alone
