criteria.applicability: Applies when the product ships a default-bearing runtime surface (ports, bind addresses, credentials, debug endpoints, transport security, file permissions, healthcheck semantics); resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (deployment-model) when no shipped surface carries an operator-facing default
criteria.expected: Shipped defaults pass least-privilege review: ports, bind addresses, credentials, debug endpoints, transport security, file permissions, and healthcheck semantics match documented operator obligations
criteria.method: Defaults sweep: read each shipped default from committed configuration, schema defaults, or code constants - the shipped value is what applies when the operator supplies no override, never a documented or intended value; classify each surface SAFE (exposes nothing sensitive without operator action), REVIEW (safe only once the operator acts, and documented when a committed operator obligation names it), or UNSAFE (exposes a sensitive surface on the shipped path: a wildcard bind on a listening or privileged surface, a shipped credential, or a debug endpoint enabled by default)
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED shipped default values and documented operator obligations; secret-bearing source is measured by SEC-SECRET - this criterion counts only shipped default values; a surface whose shipped value cannot be determined from committed configuration or constants is recorded unresolved, and the criterion resolves UNKNOWN when no named default surface can be resolved

levels.PASS: The sweep returns zero UNSAFE defaults and every REVIEW default is documented as an operator obligation
levels.P75: 1-2 REVIEW defaults, each documented as an operator obligation
levels.P50: An UNSAFE default on a surface the shipped path does not expose, or at least one REVIEW default carrying no documented operator obligation
levels.FAIL: An UNSAFE default exposed on the shipped path: a wildcard bind on a privileged or listening surface, a shipped credential, or a debug endpoint enabled by default

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: A documented path takes the product from source to running: documented build, run, and deploy steps resolve to real definitions, prerequisites are named, and every manual step in the release path is documented
criteria.method: Resolve every documented build, run, and deploy command to a file or definition; census documented prerequisites against manifests; list the manual steps the release path requires and check each is documented; doc-code drift on non-deploy surfaces is measured by MNT-DOCSYNC and excluded here
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED documentation resolved to files and definitions; evaluates the documented path, not a completed deployment - a recorded build or provisioning on the intended target is required for a verified-deployability claim

levels.PASS: Every documented step resolves to a real definition, prerequisites are named, and manual release steps are documented
levels.P75: The path resolves end to end with at most 2 minor mismatches (a renamed option or a stale path that still resolves)
levels.P50: A documented step points at a non-existent target, a prerequisite is undocumented, or release manual steps are undocumented
levels.P25: Only half the journey is documented: a build path without run or deploy steps, or a deploy procedure with no reproducible build behind it
levels.FAIL: No documented path from source to a running deployment exists where the delivery model requires one

criteria.applicability: Applies to every deployable component of the owning project; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (census-none) only when the automation census for the owning project records none - member crates inherit the workspace root's census when they ship no automation of their own, so a member crate under a signals or external census workspace is scored, never N/A on its own absent census; under an external census it stays applicable for what the external pointer establishes
criteria.expected: An automated pipeline definition builds every deployable component from source, and external workflow and action references follow pin discipline
criteria.method: Census pipeline and CI definitions; verify they build each deployable component from source; run the pin-discipline check per references/stacks/github-actions.md - every third-party uses: reference pinned to a commit SHA or a trusted-publisher versioned tag, mutable refs recorded
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED pipeline definitions; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (census-none) when the owning project's automation census is none, member crates inheriting the workspace root's census when they ship no automation of their own; under an external census it scores only what the external pointer establishes; UNKNOWN when pipeline definitions exist in tree but cannot be read

levels.PASS: A committed pipeline definition builds every deployable component from source and every third-party action or step reference is pinned to a commit SHA or a trusted-publisher versioned tag
levels.P75: The pipeline builds the product with at most 2 unpinned or floating third-party references, all outside release steps
levels.P50: The pipeline skips a deployable component, carries 3 or more floating third-party references, or a mutable third-party ref sits on a release step
levels.FAIL: Envisaged-automation signals exist but no pipeline definition is present, or the committed pipeline does not build the product

criteria.applicability: Applies to every deployable component of the owning project, covering the forward promotion path only - the revert and rollback mechanism is scored under the operational-safety criterion (OPS-REVERT) and stays out of this criterion's levels; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (census-none) only when the automation census for the owning project records none - member crates inherit the workspace root's census when they ship no automation of their own
criteria.expected: Releases follow a defined automated path: versioned immutable artifacts are produced and promoted across environments, and manual steps are minimal and documented
criteria.method: Trace the release path in pipeline and infrastructure definitions: artifact production with versioned identity, promotion steps per environment, and the deploy mechanism; census the manual steps and check each is documented; blast-radius-limiting patterns (staged, canary, blue-green) count toward the promoted-path verdict where the topology supports them
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED release and promotion definitions; resolves NOT_APPLICABLE (census-none) when the owning project's automation census is none, member crates inheriting the workspace root's census; an external census scores only what the pointer establishes; UNKNOWN when release or promotion definitions exist but their promotion behavior cannot be read

levels.PASS: Committed pipeline or infrastructure definitions produce versioned artifacts and promote them across the declared environments, with manual steps named and documented
levels.P50: Committed automation produces artifacts but promotion or deploy steps are manual, undocumented, or inconsistent across declared environments
levels.FAIL: Releases are entirely manual and undocumented where automation is required, or no committed definition carries a path from artifact to environment

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject declares scale or performance requirements or the deployment model implies a scale expectation - a service or multi-user product always applies; N/A only for a deployment model carrying no scale expectation at all, such as a single-user local utility
criteria.expected: Every declared scale, latency, throughput, availability, or concurrency requirement carries a quantified target with unit and threshold
criteria.method: Census the declared non-functional requirements in requirements, design, and deployment documents; record a target or NOT SPECIFIED per claimed quality
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED declared targets; an unstated target is NOT SPECIFIED, never inferred from mechanism descriptions or enforced limits in code; UNKNOWN only when no requirements, design, or deployment document can be inspected at all - a completed census always resolves a level

levels.PASS: Every declared scale or performance requirement in the census carries a quantified target with unit and threshold; an enforced limit in code is not required at this criterion
levels.P75: At least half of the declared requirements carry a quantified target with unit and threshold; every remainder is recorded NOT SPECIFIED by name
levels.P50: At least one declared requirement carries a quantified target and fewer than half do
levels.FAIL: The census finds declared scale or performance requirements and none carries a quantified target with unit and threshold, or the census finds no declared requirement where the deployment model implies a scale expectation; an enforced code limit without a declared target never substitutes

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject has request paths or replicated components a scaling model could govern; N/A for a deployment model that cannot carry a scale model, such as a single-component library or one-shot converter with no request paths
criteria.expected: The declared scaling model (horizontal or vertical, statelessness, partitioning, redundancy) is consistent with inspected state handling on request paths
criteria.method: Trace shared mutable state, local-disk affinity, and singleton coordination across request paths and replicated components; compare with the declared scaling model or record NOT SPECIFIED
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED state flow across request paths; a DECLARED scaling claim never closes the criterion alone; UNKNOWN only when request-path source cannot be inspected at all - an undeclared model with inspectable state handling resolves P50 or FAIL, never UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: A scaling model is declared and no inspected state pattern contradicts it - every traced request-path state pattern is consistent with the declared model, or no replication requirement is declared and no state pattern would block replication
levels.P50: No scaling model is declared and no inspected state pattern contradicts replication; the model is recorded NOT SPECIFIED
levels.FAIL: At least one inspected state pattern contradicts the declared or required model: in-process session or request state, local-disk affinity, or singleton coordination sits on a path the deployment model requires to replicate, with the contradicting pattern named

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Every enumerated resource consumer - request concurrency, connection pools, worker queues, caches, and buffers - carries a finite bound enforced in code or configuration
criteria.method: Census resource consumers on and off request paths; record a bound or UNBOUNDED per consumer, counting a framework default only when wired and cited
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED bound per enumerated consumer; an injected but unconsulted limit is configuration drift, not a bound; UNKNOWN only when no source or configuration can be inspected at all - a completed census with UNBOUNDED verdicts always resolves a level

levels.PASS: Every enumerated resource consumer carries an enforced finite bound verified in code or wired configuration
levels.P50: At least one enumerated consumer is unbounded, every unbounded consumer is named, and each sits off request and unbounded-growth paths
levels.FAIL: At least one unbounded consumer sits on a request path or grows without limit per request - unbounded-memory class when client input drives the growth

criteria.applicability: Applies when at least one latency or throughput target is declared or the deployment model implies one; N/A when no performance target is declared and none is implied by the deployment model
criteria.expected: Every declared latency or throughput target is verified by measurement under a defined workload
criteria.method: Pair each declared performance target with measured evidence: a committed benchmark or load-test artifact, or a commissioned run under an executed evidence mode
criteria.sufficiency: MEASURED evidence per the Claim Sufficiency concurrency/latency row - defined workload, environment, warmup, duration, error budget, percentile target; a mechanism description never substitutes; under source-only this criterion resolves UNKNOWN only when no committed measurement artifact and no measurable benchmark or load-test harness exist - a present-but-stale artifact grades P25 or lower, never UNKNOWN, and a current committed artifact counts as DECLARED and reaches at most P50

levels.PASS: Measured evidence under a defined workload meets every declared latency and throughput target
levels.P50: Measured evidence covers only a strict subset of declared targets with each unverified target named, or coverage rests entirely on current DECLARED committed measurement artifacts
levels.P25: A committed measurement artifact exists but is stale - it predates the current target set, environment, or measured revision - so no declared target is verified against the current state
levels.FAIL: Measured or reported evidence shows a declared target violated

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject exposes externally reachable operations on protected resources; N/A when the deployment model has no externally reachable protected operations, and a public-by-design endpoint needs a cited design basis or it counts unprotected
criteria.expected: Every externally reachable operation on a protected resource enforces principal and scope authorization on every path that can reach the resource, including result filtering for tenant, ownership, and tombstone constraints
criteria.method: Per-entry-point operation matrix built from registration sites (routes, handlers, listeners, protocol and tool registrations); an authorization verdict per row covering every sibling path to the same resource
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED trace for every registered entry point per the Claim Sufficiency authorization-isolation row; the existence of a permission helper is insufficient; UNKNOWN only when entry-point registrations cannot be enumerated or inspected at all - an unverifiable path records a coverage-gap verdict, not an assumption of enforcement

levels.PASS: Every enumerated state-changing entry point enforces an authorization decision with an inspected check cited per entry point, and every sibling path to the same protected resource enforces the same decision and result filtering
levels.P25: Enforcement is confirmed on the checked entry points but the census records at least one confirmed coverage defect short of a bypass: an unverified secondary or sibling path, or a path where enforcement is bypassable with no confirmed reachable bypass
levels.FAIL: At least one confirmed reachable bypass exists - an externally reachable path to a protected operation with no enforced authorization decision (missing-authz-state-change or auth-bypass class)

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject accepts untrusted input on any surface, network or otherwise; N/A for a deployment model with no untrusted-input surface, such as a computation artifact whose inputs are entirely trusted by construction
criteria.expected: Every untrusted-input to sensitive-sink path (command, query, filesystem path, deserialization, template, protocol frame) uses a safe construction, and every endpoint mapping input to a filesystem path carries its own traversal verdict
criteria.method: Taint census: enumerate input-accepting surfaces times sink classes and record a construction verdict per reachable pair, with per-path traversal verdicts for read and write operations
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED construction per sink path; a framework claim counts only with the mechanism named and wired; UNKNOWN only when input surfaces and sinks cannot be enumerated or inspected at all

levels.PASS: Every enumerated input-to-sink path uses a safe construction (parameterized, allowlisted, or canonicalized and contained), and every filesystem-path endpoint carries its own guarded or unreachable traversal verdict
levels.P50: Every enumerated input-to-sink path uses a safe construction, but at least one named input surface lacks boundary validation or bounds with no confirmed unsafe-sink reach
levels.P25: At least one enumerated input-to-sink path lacks safe construction and is reachable only after authentication or on a non-network surface (injection or path-traversal class at HIGH bound)
levels.FAIL: At least one enumerated input-to-sink path reaches a dangerous sink unsanitized on a public or unauthenticated surface (injection, path-traversal-read, or path-traversal-write class at CRITICAL bound)

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject issues or accepts credentials, tokens, or sessions of any type; N/A for a product that issues and accepts no credentials under its deployment model
criteria.expected: Every credential, token, or session type the system issues or accepts shows a complete lifecycle - issuance, expiry, revocation, rotation, eviction, and behavior after principal removal or demotion - and each credential type is accepted only at its intended endpoint
criteria.method: Lifecycle matrix per credential type across the six stages with a code anchor per stage; a type-separation check on the claims each accepting endpoint enforces
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED per lifecycle stage per credential type; issuance and verification alone never close the criterion; UNKNOWN only when no credential type can be enumerated or its lifecycle inspected - a type with missing stages resolves a level, never UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: Every enumerated credential type shows all lifecycle stages anchored in code - expiry enforced, a revocation path, rotation or eviction, and a defined residual-access window after removal or demotion - and type claims are enforced at each accepting endpoint
levels.P50: Expiry is enforced on every credential type but at least one named type lacks revocation or rotation, or the residual-access window is undefined for at least one type
levels.P25: At least one credential type is accepted at a non-intended endpoint (type confusion), or at least one long-lived credential type carries no expiry
levels.FAIL: At least one credential type carries neither expiry nor any revocation path, or verification is absent for a credential type

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject has a public or external request surface; N/A for a deployment model with no external request surface, and limits declared only at an external gateway count as DECLARED, never as wired enforcement
criteria.expected: Every public unauthenticated endpoint carries abuse resistance - rate or attempt limits, lockout or backoff - uniform failure responses that leak no account-existence oracle, and a finite bound with defined out-of-range behavior on every caller-controlled size parameter
criteria.method: Enumerate public endpoints and record an abuse verdict per endpoint; enumerate caller-controlled sizing parameters (page, size, limit, depth, count) and record a bounds verdict per parameter
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED per endpoint and parameter; a global middleware claim requires named wiring evidence; UNKNOWN only when public endpoints cannot be enumerated at all

levels.PASS: Every enumerated public endpoint carries a rate or attempt limit with a lockout or backoff path, every credential endpoint's failure responses are uniform with no account-existence oracle, and every caller-controlled sizing parameter carries a finite bound with defined out-of-range behavior
levels.P50: Every public credential endpoint carries a limit and lockout or backoff, but at least one named secondary public endpoint has no abuse control or at least one named sizing parameter is unbounded (unbounded-memory exposure)
levels.P25: At least one credential endpoint leaks an enumeration oracle through distinguishable failure responses, or at least one credential endpoint lacks limit, lockout, and backoff while its peers are defended
levels.FAIL: No public credential endpoint carries any rate limit, lockout, or backoff - missing-rate-limit-auth class across the whole credential surface

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: No secret material sits in the tracked tree, every credential reference resolves through a chain that never terminates in a committed literal or insecure default, and no secret reaches process arguments, logs, or error output
criteria.method: Secret-shape census over the whole tracked tree; a fallback-chain trace for every credential reference through its resolution order; an argv and logging census for secret-bearing values
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED census plus a completed chain trace per reference; a secret store's existence is insufficient without each resolution order traced; UNKNOWN only when the tracked tree cannot be census-inspected at all - a reference whose chain is untraced counts as an open coverage item, not as a PASS

levels.PASS: The secret-shape census over the whole tracked tree finds no secret material, every traced credential-resolution chain terminates in environment, vault, or operator input, and no supported path places a secret in argv, logs, or error output
levels.P25: The census finds no committed secret material, but at least one traced chain terminates in a weak fallback - a config-file literal default, a world-readable credential file, or a secret-bearing argv path (argv-secret or weak-hash-low-entropy class)
levels.FAIL: The census finds at least one item of committed secret material or a plaintext credential store in the tracked tree (committed-secret class)

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject has at least one trust boundary - a listener, entry point, or external flow in the data-flow model; N/A for a deployment model with no trust boundary, such as a library executing entirely inside the caller's trust domain
criteria.expected: Every trust boundary is enumerated, all six STRIDE categories are examined per boundary, and every material threat carries an evidenced mitigating control
criteria.method: Boundary census from listeners, entry points, and external flows from the data-flow model; a six-category STRIDE pass per boundary with a mitigation trace per identified threat
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED control per identified threat; a STRIDE enumeration without boundary and flow anchors is collection, not mitigation evidence; UNKNOWN only when boundaries cannot be enumerated from listeners and flows - an unexamined category at an enumerated boundary resolves a level, never UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: Every enumerated trust boundary carries a six-category STRIDE examination, and every identified material threat is mitigated by an inspected control
levels.P50: Boundary enumeration is complete and every boundary shows all six categories examined, but at least one named material threat's mitigating control is present yet unverified, or exactly one category is unexamined at one named boundary
levels.P25: At least one named material threat has no mitigating control at a boundary reachable only after authentication
levels.FAIL: At least one named material threat has no mitigating control at a public or unauthenticated boundary

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Every material data category the product stores or transmits carries a recorded classification: purpose, storage location, recipients, and retention or policy basis
criteria.method: Enumerate data categories from models, schemas, and storage code; reconcile the set against recorded inventories in documentation or code annotations; an unrecorded code-level category counts unclassified
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED category census reconciled with DECLARED records; an inventory document without a matching code census does not close coverage; UNKNOWN only when models, schemas, and storage code cannot be inspected at all

levels.PASS: Every enumerated data category carries a recorded classification - purpose, storage location, recipients, and retention or policy basis - reconciled against the code-level census
levels.P50: Every personal or sensitive category is recorded with purpose and basis, and at least one non-sensitive category is unrecorded with each gap category named
levels.FAIL: At least one personal or sensitive data category has no recorded purpose or basis

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject stores personal or regulated data categories - the trigger is a personal or regulated data handling surface, not the presence of any stored data; N/A for products storing no personal or regulated data
criteria.expected: Every stored personal or regulated data category has a bounded lifetime enforced by a TTL, expiry job, deletion path, or archival mechanism in code or configuration
criteria.method: Per-category check for an enforced bound and a deletion-path trace through each store that holds the category
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED enforcement per category; a DECLARED retention policy alone never establishes the bound; UNKNOWN only when the stores holding each category cannot be inspected at all

levels.PASS: Every stored personal or sensitive category carries an enforced bound - TTL, expiry job, deletion path, or archival mechanism verified in code or configuration
levels.P50: An enforced bound or working deletion path exists for at least one stored category, and every unbounded category is enumerated by name
levels.FAIL: No stored personal or sensitive category has an enforced bound or deletion path

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject stores personal data and a data-rights regime plausibly applies - the trigger is a personal or user-data handling surface, not the presence of any data; N/A for products holding no personal data or where no rights regime plausibly applies
criteria.expected: Where the product holds personal data and a data-rights regime plausibly applies, export and erasure paths exist and reach every in-scope store, including derived stores such as caches, indexes, and backups the product controls
criteria.method: Enumerate personal-data stores including derived stores; trace the export and erasure capability for each and verify deletion is not confined to the source record
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED capability path per store; a settings label or policy statement without a reachable path is insufficient; UNKNOWN only when stores cannot be enumerated or regime applicability is undetermined rather than absent - an undetermined regime resolves UNKNOWN with the counsel question recorded, never N/A

levels.PASS: Export and erasure paths are traced to every in-scope personal-data store, including each controlled derived store such as caches, indexes, and backups
levels.P50: Erasure reaches the primary store but at least one enumerated derived store lacks a propagation path, or export is absent for at least one named personal-data category
levels.FAIL: No erasure path exists for held personal data where a rights regime plausibly applies

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject performs security-relevant operations - administrative actions, role or lifecycle changes, authentication events, or permitted actions without an authenticated principal; N/A for a deployment model with no security-relevant operations, such as a product with no auth boundary and no sensitive actions
criteria.expected: Every enumerated security-relevant operation - administrative operations, role and lifecycle changes, authentication events, and permitted actions without an authenticated principal - emits an audit record holding actor, timestamp, and before-and-after state, with no silent audit-write failure and attribution only from trusted sources
criteria.method: Enumerate security-relevant operations and reconcile against the instrumented set; per-record quality check on captured state, write-reliability path, and attribution source
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED instrumentation per operation; the presence of a logging framework is insufficient; UNKNOWN only when security-relevant operations cannot be enumerated or inspected at all

levels.PASS: Every enumerated security-relevant operation is instrumented, every record holds actor, timestamp, and before-and-after state, no audit-write failure can pass silently, and attribution derives only from trusted sources
levels.P50: Every enumerated operation is instrumented but at least one record carries a named quality gap - missing before-and-after state, attribution from an untrusted source, or a silent audit-write failure path
levels.P25: At least one enumerated security-relevant operation emits no audit record, with each uninstrumented operation named
levels.FAIL: No enumerated security-relevant operation emits an audit record

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject emits outbound flows carrying personal or usage data - telemetry, analytics, or third-party calls on a user-data handling surface; N/A for products with no outbound personal or usage-data flows, where the presence of any data at rest does not trigger the criterion
criteria.expected: Every outbound flow carrying personal or usage data to a third party or telemetry endpoint is opt-in or carries a recorded basis, and each such flow is disclosed
criteria.method: Census outbound data paths such as telemetry, analytics, and third-party calls carrying user data; record a consent or basis verdict and a disclosure verdict per flow
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED flow census with a consent gate or DECLARED basis per flow; a global privacy policy without a per-flow verdict is insufficient; UNKNOWN only when outbound data paths cannot be enumerated at all

levels.PASS: Every enumerated outbound personal or usage-data flow is opt-in or carries a recorded basis, and every such flow is disclosed
levels.P50: Every enumerated flow carries a basis, but at least one named flow is undisclosed or fires before consent resolves
levels.FAIL: At least one enumerated outbound personal-data flow is silent - no consent, no recorded basis, and no disclosure

criteria.applicability: always applies
criteria.expected: Every externally reachable operation and every failure path emits a leveled, structured record through a logging facility, and no failure path discards the error unrecorded
criteria.method: Census entry points and failure paths; record a logging verdict per item and census swallow points such as empty handlers or discarded exceptions
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED logging call per enumerated path; a logging library dependency without call sites is insufficient; UNKNOWN only when entry points and failure paths cannot be enumerated at all

levels.PASS: Every enumerated operation and failure path emits a leveled structured record, and the swallow census finds no empty handler or discarded exception
levels.P50: At least half of the enumerated paths emit records, and every named gap is an unstructured record or a swallowed failure rather than a fully silent operation
levels.P25: Fewer than half of the enumerated operations emit any record, or an entire named subsystem is silent
levels.FAIL: No logging facility exists, or no enumerated path emits a record

criteria.applicability: Applies when the deployment model runs an operated long-running component or declares health or load signals - a service with operators always applies; N/A for short-lived products with no metric expectation, such as one-shot batch jobs or libraries consumed in-process
criteria.expected: Every declared health or load signal - request counts, error rates, latency, queue and resource gauges as appropriate to the product - is instrumented, and a long-running deployment exposes a health or liveness surface
criteria.method: Enumerate declared health signals and map each to instrumentation call sites or metric definitions; check the health surface for long-running subjects
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED instrumentation per signal; mechanism-brand claims and unused telemetry dependencies are insufficient; UNKNOWN only when declared signals cannot be enumerated or instrumentation cannot be inspected - where no signal is declared and the component is long-running, the health-surface check alone decides the level

levels.PASS: Every declared key signal maps to an instrumentation call site or metric definition, and every long-running component exposes a health or liveness surface
levels.P50: At least half of the declared signals are instrumented with named call sites, or the health surface is missing for at least one long-running component
levels.P25: Only framework-default metrics exist and no product-specific signal is instrumented
levels.FAIL: No metrics instrumentation exists anywhere in the subject

criteria.applicability: Applies when requests cross two or more components in the deployment model - a multi-component or distributed topology; N/A for single-component products where no cross-component flow exists
criteria.expected: Every request that crosses two or more components carries a correlation or trace identifier generated at entry and propagated through every hop, including asynchronous and external calls
criteria.method: Trace the identifier from each generation site through every component boundary it must cross; record a propagation verdict per hop
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED propagation per hop; a tracing library's presence is insufficient; UNKNOWN only when component boundaries cannot be enumerated at all - a single-component product takes the deployment-model N/A, not UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: A correlation or trace identifier is generated at every enumerated entry point and propagated through every enumerated cross-component hop, including asynchronous and external calls
levels.P50: Identifiers are generated at entry and propagated through at least half of the enumerated hops, with each unpropagated hop named
levels.FAIL: No correlation mechanism exists, or identifiers are generated but dropped at every downstream boundary

criteria.applicability: Applies when the deployment model has an operated runtime with declared failure or degradation conditions - a hosted service with operators; N/A for products with no hosted runtime and no declared alerting expectation, such as libraries or one-shot tools
criteria.expected: Every declared failure or degradation condition has a committed alert rule carrying a threshold and a notification route
criteria.method: Enumerate declared alert conditions from SLO definitions, runbooks, and configuration; reconcile each against committed alert-rule artifacts with threshold and route fields
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED alert-rule artifacts; a monitoring platform name or dashboard claim is not evidence of a rule; UNKNOWN only when declared conditions cannot be enumerated at all - an empty rule set against enumerated conditions resolves FAIL, never UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: Every declared alert condition has a committed alert-rule artifact carrying a threshold field and a notification route
levels.P50: Committed rules exist for at least one declared condition but coverage is incomplete; a rule without a route counts uncovered and each uncovered condition is named
levels.FAIL: No committed alert-rule artifact exists for any declared condition

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject makes outbound or dependency calls; N/A for a deployment model with no dependency calls
criteria.expected: Every outbound or dependency call carries an explicit timeout, every retry is attempt-bounded with backoff and idempotent where side effects occur, and every non-critical dependency failure has a fallback or degraded path
criteria.method: Census dependency call sites and record a timeout verdict per site; trace each retry loop's bound, backoff, and idempotency; record a fallback verdict per non-critical dependency
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED per call site and retry loop; a resilience-library dependency without wired policies is insufficient; UNKNOWN only when dependency call sites cannot be enumerated at all

levels.PASS: Every enumerated dependency call site carries an explicit timeout, every retry loop is attempt-bounded with backoff and idempotent where side effects occur, and every non-critical dependency has a fallback or degraded path
levels.P50: Every enumerated call site has a timeout, and every named gap is confined to retry bounds, backoff, idempotency, or fallback coverage
levels.P25: At least one external dependency call site has no timeout, or one unbounded retry loop sits on a request path
levels.FAIL: No enumerated call site has a timeout and no retry is bounded; every dependency failure propagates uncontrolled

criteria.applicability: always applies

criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED merge census with the counting rule recorded when at least 5 merge commits exist, otherwise INSPECTED committed review artifacts; when the window holds fewer than 5 merge commits and no committed review artifact exists either, both proxies lack a surface and source-only resolves the criterion as UNKNOWN

levels.P50: Every reference resolves, but at least one of: a body exceeds 500 lines, a reference chain exceeds 1 level, or non-conventional directories lack recorded justification
levels.FAIL: At least 1 referenced path does not resolve to an existing file

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships non-skill agent-facing artifacts - memory files, rules directories, plugin manifests, subagent definitions, instruction files, MCP configuration, tool manifests; a subject merely read or operated on by agents, carrying no authored agent-facing artifacts, is NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model
criteria.expected: Every discovered non-skill agent-facing artifact - memory files, rules directories, plugin manifests, subagent definitions, instruction files, MCP configuration - conforms to its format baseline: valid structure, required fields present, resolvable imports, paths, and globs, no dead patterns, no deprecated variants, no plaintext secrets in env blocks; N/A when the subject carries no non-skill agent-facing artifacts
criteria.method: Enumerate non-skill artifacts; apply each format's checkable constraints from the baseline; separate hard-constraint violations from functional gaps
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED artifacts against each format's recorded baseline; an artifact in an unrecognized format is recorded uncheckable, and when every discovered artifact is uncheckable source-only resolves the criterion as UNKNOWN; a plaintext secret in an env block is a hard-constraint violation while the secret itself is a security finding

levels.PASS: Every discovered artifact conforms to every checkable constraint of its format
levels.P50: Artifacts parse and function but at least 1 gap exists - a dead glob or applyTo pattern, a deprecated variant left alongside, a missing recommended field, or conflicting instructions across formats
levels.FAIL: At least 1 artifact is invalid or violates a hard constraint - invalid manifest JSON, a manifest without name, missing required frontmatter, or a plaintext secret in an env block

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships a declared structured agent-guidance set - more than a lone thin entry file; a subject merely read by agents, or carrying only a thin single entry file, is NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model
criteria.expected: A declared agent-guidance set resolves into a coherent topology - resolvable entry route, exactly one index of record, declared roles resolving to existing paths, recorded topic owners, restricted directories carrying read-boundary statements; N/A when the subject carries no structured guidance set (a lone thin entry file at most)
criteria.method: Enumerate the guidance set; trace the entry route from each entry file; locate authority declarations; resolve every declared role to a path; check owner selection, restricted-directory statements, vendored-document markers, and execution policy
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED documents and resolved paths; absence of structure is an observation, not a verdict - the criterion applies only to a declared set; when the set's documents cannot be inspected, source-only resolves the criterion as UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: The entry route resolves from every entry file, exactly one index of record exists, every declared role resolves to an existing path, each topic has a recorded owner or explicit N/A, restricted directories carry read-boundary statements, and no conflicting or stale guidance exists
levels.P50: The set functions but carries at least 1 gap - a second authority declaration, duplicated rule text across owners, unrecorded consolidation, a stale vendored document, an undeclared restricted directory, or an unrecorded execution policy
levels.FAIL: The entry route is broken or circular, two documents conflict over the same rules with no recorded precedence, or documents present boilerplate or nonexistent paths as authoritative

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships authored skills with bundled files; a subject merely read or operated on by agents, carrying no authored skills, is NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model
criteria.expected: The census over every bundled skill file finds no security-surface risk pattern - unexpected network calls, file access outside declared scope, tool invocations exceeding allowed-tools, instructions fetched from mutable external sources, or unexplained sensitive-data access; N/A when the subject carries no authored skills
criteria.method: Census every bundled file (SKILL.md, scripts, resources) for the named risk patterns; reconcile each hit against the skill's stated purpose and declared allowed-tools
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED bundled files reconciled against the stated purpose; the declared purpose bounds what counts as unexpected; when bundled files cannot be inspected (opaque or unreadable resources that could carry the named patterns), source-only resolves the criterion as UNKNOWN rather than PASS

levels.PASS: Zero risk-pattern hits, or every hit is inside the declared scope and consistent with the stated purpose and declared tools
levels.P50: At least 1 risk-pattern hit sits outside the declared scope but consistent with the stated purpose, including documented fetches of mutable external content
levels.FAIL: At least 1 hit sits outside the stated purpose or declared tools - instructions fetched from mutable external URLs not required by the purpose, tool invocations exceeding allowed-tools, or unexplained sensitive-data access

criteria.applicability: Applies when the subject ships two or more authored skills; a subject with fewer than two authored skills, or one merely read by agents without authored agent-facing artifacts, is NOT_APPLICABLE via deployment-model
criteria.expected: A multi-skill subject is a coherent collection: every authored skill declares a unique name, every authored skill is listed in a catalog or index, and sibling skills share layout conventions; N/A when fewer than two authored skills are in scope
criteria.method: Compare declared names across skills; locate the catalog or index and reconcile it against the discovered skill inventory; compare directory layouts
criteria.sufficiency: INSPECTED frontmatter names, catalog content, and layouts; installed or out-of-scope skills do not enter the comparison; when the authored-skill inventory cannot be completed, source-only resolves the criterion as UNKNOWN

levels.PASS: All names are unique, every authored skill is catalogued, and layouts are consistent
levels.P50: All names are unique; the catalog is absent or incomplete, or layouts diverge without a recorded reason
levels.FAIL: At least 2 authored skills declare the same name, or at least 1 authored skill is absent from every catalog and index

severity_anchors.condition: An unauthenticated remote caller reaches an operation the design declares authenticated
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (authentication bypass is named critical-class impact) x likelihood HIGH (trivially triggered by any remote client) = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: The bypass is reachable only under a non-default configuration, a rare sequencing, or a local-only surface
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL x likelihood LOW (unusual combination of conditions required) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: An unauthenticated remote caller reaches a state-changing operation with no principal or scope check
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (unbounded data mutation) x likelihood HIGH = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: An authenticated principal reaches a state-changing operation outside its granted object or scope set
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (major function or integrity loss bounded by the credential) x likelihood MEDIUM (requires a valid principal) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: A remote caller - unauthenticated or authenticated - can write files outside the intended root
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (arbitrary write leads to host compromise or data destruction) x likelihood MEDIUM or HIGH = CRITICAL either way

severity_anchors.condition: The write primitive is reachable only from a local or trusted-position input
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL x likelihood LOW (attacker must already hold local position) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: A remote unauthenticated caller can read files that hold credentials or secret material
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (data breach) x likelihood HIGH = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: A remote read escapes the intended tree but reaches only application data without credential material, or requires an authenticated principal
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (contained data disclosure) x likelihood MEDIUM = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: A remote surface ships with default or well-known credentials that are not forced to change on first use
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (equivalent to an authentication bypass) x likelihood HIGH (credential value is public) = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: A query, command, or template injection is reachable from unauthenticated remote input with demonstrated sink reach
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (data breach or code execution) x likelihood HIGH = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: The injection is reachable only from authenticated or second-order input, or the sink is constrained (blind or bounded)
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (constrained compromise) x likelihood MEDIUM = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: A live credential committed to the repository grants remote access to a system or dataset
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (credential replay leads to breach) x likelihood HIGH (usable by anyone with read access) = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: A live secret is placed on a process argument list or other surface readable by co-tenant processes on the host
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (credential disclosure to co-tenant actors) x likelihood MEDIUM (requires host access) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: A low-entropy secret such as a password, PIN, or short token is stored under an unsalted fast hash
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (credential compromise once the store is exposed) x likelihood MEDIUM (requires the store to leak first) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: A remote authentication or token endpoint accepts unbounded attempts with no lockout or throttling
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (enables credential brute force) x likelihood MEDIUM (requires attacker interest) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: Throttling is absent but a compensating control exists (account lockout, MFA, or monitored alerts)
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact MEDIUM (contained by the compensating control) x likelihood MEDIUM = MEDIUM

severity_anchors.condition: A non-loopback listener carrying credentials or sensitive data accepts plaintext by shipped default
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (session or credential interception) x likelihood MEDIUM (requires network position) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: Certificate verification is disabled in the shipped default or documented configuration of an outbound connection
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (man-in-the-middle against the channel) x likelihood MEDIUM (requires network position) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: Plaintext is confined to a loopback or unix-socket binding inside one trust domain
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact MEDIUM x likelihood LOW (requires local position) = LOW

severity_anchors.condition: An unhandled panic or abort is reachable from remote request input in a long-running service with no supervisor or restart bound
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (full outage) x likelihood HIGH (trivially triggered) = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: The same reachable panic is bounded by a supervisor, restart, or worker isolation that limits the blast radius
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact MEDIUM (contained outage or degraded capacity) x likelihood HIGH = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: Unauthenticated client input drives unbounded memory growth with no size, count, or time bound
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (outage via exhaustion) x likelihood MEDIUM (sustained or crafted input needed) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: Acknowledged writes are lost on an ordinary crash - no fsync, journal, or durability record on the write path
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (data loss named critical-class impact) x likelihood MEDIUM (requires crash timing) = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: An advertised core capability - one the product exists to provide - is backed by a stub, fixed return, or unimplemented path
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (sole function absent) x likelihood HIGH (always manifests) = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: A secondary advertised feature is stubbed while core workflows remain functional
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact MEDIUM (degraded function) x likelihood HIGH (always manifests) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: An advertised core journey fails at a producer or consumer hop and cannot complete end to end
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL (core function loss) x likelihood HIGH (every attempt fails) = CRITICAL

severity_anchors.condition: No test exercises an advertised core workflow, so regressions escape undetected
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (undetected core regression) x likelihood MEDIUM (realizes on a future change) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: A distributed or published work carries no license declaration of any kind
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (consumers cannot lawfully adopt the work) x likelihood MEDIUM (realizes on distribution or reuse) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: A dependency carries a KNOWN_APPLICABLE advisory whose vulnerable path is reachable in the subject
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact HIGH (per advisory impact on the reachable path) x likelihood MEDIUM (exploit position required) = HIGH

severity_anchors.condition: The advisory's impact is critical-class and the vulnerable path is reachable by an unauthenticated remote caller
severity_anchors.rationale: Impact CRITICAL x likelihood MEDIUM or HIGH = CRITICAL
